kuvaus.en:
Our understanding of the universe and all modern technology is based on advances made in scientific research over approximately the last 100 years. The operation of computers and mobile phones relies fully on quantum mechanical principles, and the nature of matter in the universe has been unveiled by studies in particle physics, astronomy and cosmology. New exciting discoveries are constantly made and will affect our future. For instance, studies on quantum information combined with the development of new materials are just about to open the doors for quantum computing, and the analysis by artificial intelligence of big data will lead to new ways to cure disease.  

The Bachelor's Programme in Science is designed to provide students with an interdisciplinary education that encompasses various fields of science such as mathematics, statistics, physics, chemistry, and computer/data science. The Programme is geared towards equipping students with the knowledge and skills required to work at the forefront of exciting basic research and application development. The curriculum is structured to ensure that students receive a solid foundation in the core disciplines of science, while also allowing them to specialize in a particular field of interest.  

Hands-on learning experiences, including laboratory experiments and computer simulations, are integral to the Programme. Students will learn how to critically analyse data, design and conduct experiments, and communicate their findings to others. The interdisciplinary nature of the Programme will enable students to develop a broad perspective on science, and to appreciate the interconnections between different fields of study. This expertise gives our graduates a competitive edge in the job market, as they are well-prepared to tackle complex, real-world problems that require knowledge across multiple scientific domains.  

Upon graduation, students are ready to pursue a variety of careers in science, including research and development in academia, industry, and government.

Further information about the studies are on the bachelor’s programme website.

osaamistavoitteet.en:
Graduates of the programme will have developed:

  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, enabling them to identify, formulate, and solve complex scientific problems across disciplines.
  • Quantitative and computational skills, including the ability to apply mathematical models, statistical reasoning, and programming techniques to analyze scientific data.
  • Scientific literacy, including the ability to read, evaluate, and synthesize scientific literature and to understand the broader impact of scientific discoveries.
  • Hands-on research skills, such as designing and conducting experiments or simulations, analyzing results, and drawing evidence-based conclusions.
  • Effective communication abilities, including presenting scientific results clearly in written, visual, and oral formats to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
  • Collaborative and project management skills, developed through interdisciplinary group work and practical lab or coding projects.
  • Adaptability and independent learning, preparing students to approach unfamiliar scientific questions with confidence and to continue their studies at the MSc level or beyond.
  • Ethical and societal awareness, including understanding the role of science in addressing global challenges and the responsible use of scientific knowledge and data.

kuvaus.en: There are no tuition fee waivers for the bachelor’s degree programme. However, in case you graduate from your bachelor’s degree by the target duration of your degree with a required GPA and continue to a master’s programme available for graduates from your programme, you will be awarded a tuition fee waiver for your master’s degree. With minimum GPA 3,8/5 you qualify for 100 % tuition fee waiver and with 3,4-3,7/5 you qualify for 50 % tuition fee waiver. Waiver covers also the second study year of your Master's degree in case you have completed at least 55 credits during first academic year.

maksullisuusKuvaus.en: Tuition fee per year for non-EU/EEA citizens. No tuition fee for EU/EEA citizens.

teksti.en:
The programme is aimed at students who are curious about science and want to build an interdisciplinary understanding across several scientific fields. During the first part of the programme, all students follow a common curriculum that provides a solid foundation in mathematics, programming, and the basics of scientific thinking. After this shared starting point, students choose one of four study tracks: physics, chemistry, mathematics & statistics, or computer & data science.  

Each study track offers a high degree of flexibility, allowing students to tailor their studies by including elective courses from the other tracks. This structure enables students to deepen their expertise in one field while also exploring connections across disciplines. The programme is ideal for students who want to combine their main area of interest with a broad scientific perspective.  

Graduates will be well-prepared to continue their studies at the MSc level and pursue careers that value versatile scientific knowledge. To succeed in the programme, students should have a strong background in mathematics, science, and English.
Completing this study programme will grant the students the title Bachelor of Science (BSc).

Graduates of the Bachelor's Programme in Science have a bright employment outlook, with many excellent opportunities available to them in various industries and research institutes. In Finland and EU countries, the Programme’s alumni can find employment in IT companies, nanoscience, and chemical industries, among others. The programme equips students with both subject knowledge and skills, and soft skills such as presenting and reporting skills, which are very important in the working world. Continuing with a MSc degree further expands a wide selection of expert positions in industry, research institutes and the finance sector. MSc graduates also have a very good chance to continue in fundamental research in university or research institute PhD programmes.

The Bachelor's programme comprises of 180 credits, which can be completed in three years. The degree includes:  

  • 15-30 credits of mandatory studies in basic mathematics, basic computer science, and statistics  
  • 25 credits of mandatory common studies: language and communication skills, career orientation and professional skills, ICT skills and a group work course introducing modern science topics studied at the Faculty. Language studies comprise 10 credits: 4 credits of academic and professional communication and 6 credits of basic courses in Finnish and/or Swedish (for students with Finnish or Swedish as their language of secondary education, 3 credits of Finnish and 3 credits of Swedish at an advanced level)  
  • 60-105 credits of study track specific basic and intermediate studies, including a final seminar (4 cr) and bachelor's thesis (6 cr)  
  • 35-50 credits of other, freely chosen courses according to your study track and personal study plan  


In the Studies Service, you can explore the degree structure, content and learning outcomes from the level of the degree programme to individual courses. Full degree structure in the Studies Service.

During the first fall semester, all students receive a foundation in university-level mathematics and basic programming skills. After this, they can choose a study track, with second- and third-year university-level courses offered in mathematics and statistics, computer/data science, physics, and chemistry. It is possible to either deepen the studies in one of these study tracks or to combine studies of two or three tracks to get a truly multidisciplinary education.

The study tracks:  

  • Chemistry: Would you like to contribute to finding novel solutions in circular economy, future energy sources, food production, clean water and air, health care, or making use of carbon dioxide? These are examples of the topics that will employ a number of chemists in the near future. In the chemistry study track, you get to learn about the fundamental concepts and modern experimental methods of chemistry. These will allow you to continue in MSc towards specialization in any of the different research directions of chemistry, either with a practical or theoretical view. In addition to the common basic and subject studies in chemistry (65 cr + thesis and seminar 10 cr), you can choose elective courses that help you train towards your own interests. After graduation with your BSc degree, you will have the direct option to continue at UH for example in the Master’s Programme in Chemistry, the Master’s Programme in Materials Research, the Master’s Programme in Theoretical and Computational Methods, or the Master's Programme in Meteorology, Atmospheric and Climate-System Sciences.  
     
  • Computer and data science: The students in the study track of computer and data science acquire the skills to build modern software both by doing hands-on exercises and projects and by studying the fundamental ideas underlying how computers work and how they can be used efficiently. They also get an introduction to the new possibilities created by artificial intelligence and the analysis of large masses of data. Studies in mathematics are a necessary foundation for the more advanced concepts in computer science, in particular going beyond the bachelor's level. Students graduating from the study track of computer and data science can continue, for example, in the Master's Programme in Computer Science or the Master's Programme in Data Science.  

  

  • Mathematics and statistics: The mathematics and statistics study track emphasises mathematics as a science of its own and its importance in statistics. It offers an introduction both to the key concepts and methods of modern mathematics as well as a wider view on the exact world of mathematics, studying exactly defined concepts and the properties and relationships that emerge among these. In addition, the elective module offers an introduction to basics of statistical modelling, inference and computation. The study track offers a solid ground for continuing higher level studies in mathematics and statistics. Depending on the optional studies chosen, the track directs the students towards either the world of pure mathematics or mathematical statistics, with research questions arising from within theoretical settings, or towards applied mathematics or statistics where mathematical and statistical tools are used to solve questions arising in other areas such as the physical world around us. The study track gives the required prerequisites for continuing studies in the Master's Programme in Mathematics and Statistics. Including studies in computer science also makes the student eligible to continue in the Master’s Programme in Life Science Informatics or the Master’s Programme in Data Science. Including courses in physics or chemistry allows for studies in the Master’s Programme in Theoretical and Computational Methods.  

  

  • Physics: The physics study track offers a strong foundation in both classical and quantum physics, exploring how these principles explain natural phenomena and contribute to modern technologies and our understanding of the universe. After completing the common basic and subject studies (60 credits), students can tailor their course selection to align with their interests and prepare for one or more of the relevant Master's programmes. Depending on the chosen elective courses, students in the Physics track can progress toward the following Master’s programmes: Master’s Programme in Particle Physics and Astrophysical Sciences, Master’s Programme in Materials Research (which includes nanoscience and biophysics), and Master’s Programme in Theoretical and Computational Methods. Students can also prepare for interdisciplinary Master’s studies by combining Physics with other disciplines: physics+mathematics: Master’s Programme in Theoretical and Computational Methods; physics+chemistry: Master’s Programme in Chemistry, Master’s Programme in Materials Research, or Master's Programme in Meteorology, Atmospheric and Climate-System Sciences; physics+computer science: Master’s Programme in Data Science.

At the end of the degree, typically either in the fall or spring semester of the 3rd year, you will write a Bachelor's thesis, the scope of which is 6 cr. The aim of the thesis is to get a deeper understanding of a specific topic and to learn the scientific working methods and writing practices of your field. The thesis is a literature review in nature, but may also include data analysis, modelling, or experimental work. In the Mathematics and statistics, Physics, and Chemistry study tracks the writing is done individually, but you will receive support from a supervisor. In the Computer and Data science study track, the students participate in bachelor’s thesis instruction groups, and write their thesis individually or, optionally, together with a pair.

Obtaining a Bachelor of Science (BSc) degree makes you eligible to apply for various job positions that require a first-cycle academic degree.  

Admitted students are offered two possibilities for higher-level university studies: a 3-year (180 ECTS credit points) programme for a BSc degree, or a 3+2 year (180 + 120 credits) programme for both a BSc and an MSc programme. Students admitted to the Bachelor’s Programme in Science have the right, after completion of the BSc degree, to continue either directly or via application in one of the MSc programmes at the University of Helsinki. The directly-selectable programmes cover the full range of modern natural sciences from pure mathematics to chemistry.  

The Bachelor’s Programme in Science specialization (mathematics and statistics, computer and data science, physics, or chemistry) determines the eligibility of students for various MSc programmes. The Faculty of Science offers several MSc programmes, in which students can continue from their BSc degree. These programmes include Mathematics and Statistics, Life Science Informatics, Atmospheric Sciences, Particle Physics and Astrophysical Sciences, Materials Research, Theoretical and Computational Methods, Chemistry, Computer Science, and Data Science. However, each MSc programme has its own entrance requirements, and the choice of the BSc study track determines which MSc programmes the student will be able to continue in.  

The academic mentors will aid the student throughout the studies in setting up a personal study plan that ensures entrance to the desired MSc programme. In most cases, several options can be kept open until the third year. For instance, a student choosing the physics study track will be able to continue in at least the Atmospheric Sciences, Particle Physics and Astrophysical Sciences and Materials Research programmes. Courses offered in the third year of the BSc programme serve as an introduction to these MSc programmes, and the student can make their choice after taking these courses.  

In addition to the master's options in the Faculty of Science, students admitted to the Bachelor's Programme in Science, have the option, after completion of the BSc degree, to continue in the Master's Programme in Social Research at the Faculty of Social Sciences and in the Master's Programme in Linguistic Diversity and Digital Humanities at the Faculty of Arts and Master’s Programme in Geography at the Faculty of Science.

After completing a Master's degree, you can apply to a doctoral programme at the University of Helsinki and at other universities in Finland or abroad.  

For more information, please see the Doctoral Education at the University of Helsinki website.

In the Faculty of Science, the course selection is not limited to the modules offered by your own education Programme. You can choose courses from other Programmes, both within your own faculty and from the university’s other faculties.  

Thanks to cross-institutional collaboration in Finland, you can study some courses at selected Finnish universities, such as Aalto University. This can help tailor your degree according to your interests and career plans.   

Throughout studies, establishing connections with the working world is crucial. Many students work concurrently with their studies and can incorporate this experience into their degrees through the working life section of the degree. Optional entrepreneurship courses and Think Company provide avenues for developing business ideas, fostering collaboration between students, researchers, and corporate partners in various fields.  

In addition, you can participate in research projects through thesis and seminar work, i.e., concrete research work. Writing your BSc thesis in cooperation with a research group, corporation or research organisation is also a good way to improve your working-life abilities.  

The physics research at the Faculty of Science is carried out in close collaboration with leading European big science institutions such as CERN and the European Southern Observatory. Computer science at the University of Helsinki has considerable collaboration with corporations in the fields of networks, data security, data science, etc. Within the field of data security is the Intel Collaborative Research Institute (ICRI-SC). The Nokia Centre for Advanced Research (NCAR) was established in spring 2016 to promote research on data science and networks. Department of Chemistry has close connections to the Finnish Chemical Industry association, and several projects are carried out in cooperation with the enterprises in chemical, forest and semiconductor industry.

The Faculty of Science has a highly international environment, with the majority of MSc programmes taught in English, and all PhD programmes conducted in English. About 30% of the PhD researchers are foreigners, and each year around 20% of the students starting in the MSc programmes are international. In addition, the degree programmes take in close to 150 exchange students per year.  

In addition, the University of Helsinki and the Faculty of Science offer you many opportunities for international activities:  

  • Instruction in English within other education programmes  
  • International tasks within the student organisations or the student union  
  • Language courses at the Language Centre of the University of Helsinki  

You can also get information and counselling on independent international experience, such as:  

  • Student exchange at one of the exchange locations of the faculty or university  
  • Traineeships abroad

The University of Helsinki is the leading university in the country, with a strong focus on basic research and research-based education. The strongest research areas in the university include those studied at the Faculty of Science, such as atmospheric research, mathematics, data science, and materials research.   

At the Department of Chemistry, the major research focus areas are Energy, Materials, and Health&Environment. These include themes such as catalysis research, new materials for the semiconductor industry, and medical applications such as imaging and drug development.  

Research at the Department of Physics focuses on particle physics, astrophysics and space physics, astronomy, materials physics, nanophysics, and biophysics. The physics research at the faculty is carried out in close collaboration with the leading European big science institutions (such as CERN, ITER, and the European Southern Observatory), university hospitals, and high-performance computing facilities (like CSC and PRACE).  

Research at the Department of Computer Science is structured into four research areas: Algorithms, Artificial Intelligence, Networks, and Software. The department hosts the Helsinki Institute for Information Technology HIIT, which is a joint research centre with Aalto University, and the Finnish Center for AI (FCAI), which is one of the national Research Council of Finland flagships.   

Research at the department of Mathematics and Statistics focuses on mathematical analysis and logic. Applications of mathematics such as inversion problems and in an area called mathematical physics are also prominent at the international level.  

Several multidisciplinary research projects are under way at the Faculty of Science, which are being carried out in cooperation with the research institutes on the science campus and with other faculties, universities, and corporations.

opetuskieletKuvaus.en:
Instruction in the Bachelor's Programme in Science is given fully in English.

Students who know Finnish or Swedish can also attend courses at the Faculty given in these languages and include these in their degree if the courses are included or mentioned in their personal study plan. However, at least 75% of the studies, including the bachelor's thesis, must be completed in English.

If you have completed or will complete by 31 August 2027 one of the above examinations, you must apply in admission group 2. If you apply based on Open University studies, you must apply in admission group 2.

nimi.en: Bachelor's Programme in Science, Admission Group 1, Bachelor and Master of Science (3 yrs + 2 yrs)

kuvaus.en:
Applications must be accompanied by the following documents submitted as instructed below:

  • Copy of the degree certificate/diploma
  • Certificate of language proficiency
  • Official score report of required SAT or ACT tests (admission group 1 only)
  • Authorised translations (if necessary)
  • A photocopy of your passport OR national identity card OR your Finnish residence permit card.

1) For further information and instructions on how to submit the required attachments, please read carefully the University’s instructions on submitting application documents.

2) If the degree serving as grounds of your application is still incomplete, you need not submit a degree certificate/diploma with the application documents. However, you must submit at the application stage your official transcript of studies from the current year or another certificate granted by your educational institution indicating the degree you are pursuing, as well as its scope and estimated completion date. The transcript or certificate must also feature the official stamp of the educational institution, and the signature, name in block letters and job title of its representative. If you are admitted, the admission decision will be conditional, and you will receive instructions with your letter of admission for submitting the degree certificate/diploma. NB! The degree must, however, be completed by 31 August 2027.

3) You must demonstrate your language proficiency in English. Please see the University’s instructions for further information on the demonstration of language proficiency.

4) The primary method to submit enclosures is to attach them to your application. However, if you are not able to do so, you may also send them via email, regular post or personally deliver the enclosures. Please see the instructions on how to submit enclosures at the application stage for more information.

5) The University of Helsinki must receive the results of required SAT or ACT tests directly from the test organiser (College Board or ACT). You must select the University of Helsinki (SAT code 0483, ACT code 8225) as the recipient of your results when registering for the test. If you have taken the test at an earlier date, you must request a report of the results to be separately submitted to the University of Helsinki. Instructions for the submission of results are available on the College Board website as well as the ACT website.
